newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones cuts bonuses for top executives.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones cuts bonuses for top executives.

text.p: Bonuses for Dow Jones & Co's top executives were cut after the company's compensation committee determined its stock performance in the past year was not satisfactory.

According to the company's proxy statement filed in advance of its April 16 annual meeting, Chairman and Chief Executive Peter Kann had his annual bonus cut to $380,000 for 1996 compared to $445,000 in the prior year.

The Independent Association of Publishers' Employees, which represents employees at Dow Jones, including its Wall Street Journal newspaper, also has put forth a stockholder proposal to create an independent review of top management and their performance.

President and Chief Operating Officer Kenneth Burenga's bonus was cut to $270,000 from $310,000; Senior Vice President Carl Valenti's was reduced to $155,000 from $220,000; and Senior Vice President Peter Skinner's dropped to $165,000 from $205,000.
Only Senior Vice President James Ottaway Jr's remained unchanged at $160,000.
The committee reported in the proxy statement that it compared Dow Jones' performance in 1996 with companies in the S&P 500 as well as the S&P's publishing and newspapers index.

"Overall, the committee determined that performance for the 1993-1996 period was less than fully satisfactory, particularly as measured by three financial criteria given significant weight by the committee: stock price performance, total stockholder return and return on equity," it said in the proxy statement.
The union-backed stockholder proposal is to be voted on at the annual meeting. The union holds 55 shares of Dow Jones' common stock and 10 shares of its Class B common stock.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk 212-859-1713))
